Article Title: Pakistan’s England nightmare deepens: 11 WTC points docked, 50% match fee fine — here’s why
Article Text:
Pakistan's Babar Azam, center, with teammates following his side's defeat to England at Edgbaston. (AP Photo)

11-point deduction and maximum fine

England complete 3-0 sweep

NEW DELHI: Pakistan’s disastrous 0-3 Test series defeat against England has been compounded by a significant over-rate penalty, with the side losing 11 World Test Championship points and being fined 50 per cent of their match fee following the Edgbaston Test.Pakistan were found to be 11 overs short of the required over-rate during the third and final Test in Birmingham, which England won by eight wickets to complete a 3-0 series sweep.“Pakistan have been hit with a pair of sanctions for maintaining a slow over-rate during the third and final ICC World Test Championship contest against England in Birmingham,” the ICC said.Ranjan Madugalle of the Emirates ICC Elite Panel of Match Referees imposed the sanction after on-field umpires Paul Reiffel and Chris Gaffaney, third umpire Allahudien Palekar and fourth umpire Russell Warren levelled the charge.Pakistan captain Babar Azam pled guilty to the offence and accepted the proposed sanction, meaning there was no need for a formal hearing.The deduction further dents Pakistan’s position at the bottom of the WTC standings, leaving them ninth with a points percentage of 4.63.Under Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, players are fined five per cent of their match fee for every over their side fails to bowl within the allotted time, with the maximum penalty capped at 50 per cent.“In accordance with Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to minimum over-rate offences, players are fined five per cent of their match fee for each over their team fails to bowl within the allotted time, with the maximum penalty capped at 50 percent of the match fee.”The 11-over shortfall also resulted in an 11-point deduction under the WTC playing conditions.“In addition, as per Article 16.11.2 of the ICC World Test Championship playing conditions, a side is penalised one point for each over short. Consequently, 11 World Test Championship points have been deducted from Pakistan’s points total,” the ICC said.The penalty adds to a miserable WTC campaign for Pakistan, who have recorded just two wins and seven defeats from nine Tests and now languish ninth in the standings.England completed the series sweep with an eight-wicket victory at Edgbaston. Pakistan were bowled out for 133 in their first innings before England posted 453, taking a 320-run lead.Pakistan fought back with 449 in their second innings, with Shan Masood scoring 95, Babar making 76 and debutant Razaullah hitting 81. Razaullah and Mohammad Abbas added 121 for the ninth wicket.But England needed only 130 and reached 130/2, with Joe Root unbeaten on 62 and Jordan Cox on 59.England had earlier won the series opener at Headingley by an innings and 103 runs and the second Test at Lord’s by 194 runs.Pakistan’s next WTC assignment comes in November when they host Sri Lanka for a two-Test series in Rawalpindi and Lahore.
Article Summary: Pakistan were found to be 11 overs short of the required over-rate during the third and final Test in Birmingham. England won by eight wickets to complete a 3-0 series sweep. Pakistan lost 11 World Test Championship points and were fined 50 per cent of their match fee.

Article Title: A coach's fasting, nod to MS Dhoni, and the 'funniest' team: Inside Ganges Grandmasters' GCL 2026 title
Article Text:
Ganges Grandmasters become GCL 2026 champions

A 'not a full-time coach' at the helm

An accidental nod to MS Dhoni

A childhood hero, now a champion teammate

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

'The funniest team' wins it finally

BENGALURU: Who doesn't love a good underdog story? Everyone does, right? Nobody had Ganges Grandmasters finishing on top of anything when Season 4 of the Global Chess League (GCL) began in Bengaluru just less than a fortnight ago. Six teams, a league stage so tight, and a final that only got decided after the very last match was played on Saturday evening.With Grandmasters like Ian Nepomniachtchi, Levon Aronian, Leinier Domínguez and Leon Luke Mendonca, and International Masters like Polina Shuvalova and Stavroula Tsolakidou, it was a diverse side, one few expected to go all the way.By Sunday, as the confetti cannons went off, it was Ganges Grandmasters, not the defending champions APL Pipers, not the team with Magnus Carlsen on the Icon board, standing at the top of the podium.7-5 remained the aggregate score by which Ganges Grandmasters beat the Pipers across the two-leg final, having drawn the first leg 3-3, where the Grandmasters played with the White pieces.With the Black, though, Ian Nepomniachtchi pounced on a positional error from Carlsen, refusing to give the world number one any route back into the game. And as the five-time world champion's position collapsed, so did the Pipers' hopes of retaining the title.Behind the scenes, however, the triumph is about so much more than a good underdog story.Adhiban Baskaran, who, by the admission of all the players in the team, played an integral role in keeping it all together throughout the campaign, is not a coach."I'm not a full-time coach, so I wanted to clarify. I am like a professional player," the 34-year-old Grandmaster told reporters on Sunday. "But this time, I was free. I didn't have any tournaments in September, so I just wanted to be part of something great."That "something great" turned into a maiden GCL title on debut as a coach, a fact Baskaran still seemed slightly stunned by."To win the GCL Season 4 on debut is amazing, and something I'm very proud of," he added.What makes his version of the story worth telling isn't the tactics or the pairings. It's what he brought into the dugout that had nothing to do with chess at all.With his humour, superstition, and a level of emotional investment, he uplifted the overall spirit of the team after a topsy-turvy start to the tournament, including two wins and two losses in the opening four games.Take the nickname, for example. Somewhere along the way, Baskaran started handing out monikers to the squad, and one of them, nevertheless, became more popular than the others.Earlier in the tournament, Greek chess player Stavroula Tsolakidou revealed that Baskaran had prepared her for a game with a file titled “Prep for the Greek Goddess!”"I was trying to come up with nicknames for everyone, and that's how I came up with this nickname, Greek Goddess," he said. It became a name that would end up being shouted across the venue by the time she clinched the title-sealing win over Koneru Humpy and picked up the Player of the Tournament award, complete with a Jawa motorbike."I didn't expect it would actually become so popular in such a short span," Baskaran admitted.Then there was the fasting. After a mid-tournament loss, Baskaran quietly made himself a promise."I didn't have breakfast, I didn't have lunch, and I told myself if the team is not winning, I will also not have dinner," he said with a smile after Sunday's victory. "And they won. So I could actually have dinner."What started as a one-off superstition calcified into a five-day ritual."I thought, okay, why fix something which doesn't break? So I started to fast every lunch. I didn't have lunch for the past five days, also with the thought that I would not have dinner if the team didn't win. But luckily, my team was always winning, and they were helping me, so I could at least have dinner," he revealed.By the end of the tournament, he was only half-joking about the toll it had taken. "My stomach is literally crying now," he remarked.Baskaran's calm in the dugout, it turns out, had a specific origin, and it arrived by text message, from his father, in the middle of the rough patch earlier in the season."After the second day, I think we lost one match," Baskaran recalled. "And my father sent me this message that, you know, you just try to be like one of your role models, Dhoni. He messaged, 'Try to be like Captain Cool, your role model.' So I was like, yeah, I will try to be like that.""In fact, I chose my (jersey) number seven for Ronaldo," he said. "But actually, Dhoni's number is also seven. So there's an inside joke about Dhoni; the credit always walks back to Dhoni."Pressed on whether that same reflexive credit-giving applied here, the way, say, cricketer Hardik Pandya once attributed India wins to Dhoni's mere presence in the dressing room, Baskaran deflected the comparison entirely."No, no. Here I feel it's because of my team," he added. "I think they played very well."Whatever the jersey number said, Baskaran's dugout stayed visibly, deliberately calm, right up until it had a trophy to celebrate.Baskaran admits that the real reason he chose to coach the GCL outfit during his time off had little to do with money, fame, or anything material."Levon (Aronian) has been my hero for as long as I can remember," Baskaran revealed. "Ever since he won the World Junior in Goa, I've been a big fan of him." Getting to coach him, rather than simply admire him from a distance, was its own reward. "Getting to understand how the players are, the psychology, how they prepare, that's something I really wanted to know. So that was the reason I wanted to be part of this team."Aronian, for his part, returned the affection when asked about Baskaran directly."He's such a friendly, such a calm and pleasant person," Aronian said after the trophy celebration. "I've known him since he was very young, even our fathers are friends."Throughout the tournament, this did not look like a group of mercenaries assembled for a tournament, as confirmed by Aronian as well."I think we have very relaxed egos, less structure in a team, and everybody can make a joke. There is no limit to jokes. I just felt like it was some family type of experience. I will treasure those days," the veteran Grandmaster admitted.Russian Grandmaster and the team's icon player Nepomniachtchi, whose demolition of Carlsen effectively won the title, echoed the same sentiment from a very different starting point, a player who admitted he'd arrived in Bengaluru unsure of his own form after a rough year of rating losses."I wasn't sure what my form was at the moment," he said. "But I was really pleasantly surprised with the atmosphere inside the team. Despite different ages, different cultures, we really found points of connection. It was always very healthy, very jokey. I think it really made the difference."Going by their social media, one can see the Ganges Grandmasters players often indulging in physical sports like padel, golf, and basketball after their gruelling round of matches in GCL. Perhaps that built the team spirit."I think it's more about team spirit," Adhiban said. "Always joking, always having fun, I would actually say we are the funniest team. Maybe that's one of the reasons."Nobody had Ganges Grandmasters in their top two.By Sunday night, the top belonged to the man who led the underdogs, now holding a trophy, still fasting, still cracking jokes in the "funniest team" of the GCL's fourth edition.
Article Summary: Ganges Grandmasters beat APL Pipers 7.7-5 in the final of the Global Chess League (GCL) in Bengaluru. The victory was the first for the team, coached by Adhiban Baskaran, who is not a full-time coach. The 34-year-old brought a level of superstition and humour to the team.

Article Title: Watch: ‘Good job sir’ — Pakistan fan praises Mohsin Naqvi after Team India snubs trophy at Women’s Asia Cup

Pakistan fan praises Mohsin Naqvi

‘Trophy chor’ chants echo after India snub presentation

Saikia explains India’s decision

NEW DELHI: India’s record eighth Women’s Asia Cup title was followed by a trophy presentation that quickly became the biggest talking point of the final — and a video from outside the Dubai International Cricket Stadium has now added another twist to the controversy.A video circulating on social media shows Asian Cricket Council president and Pakistan Cricket Board chairman Mohsin Naqvi leaving the stadium after India defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final on Sunday.As Naqvi’s car passed a Pakistan supporter filming his exit, the fan could be heard praising the PCB chief and backing his handling of the situation involving India.“Good job sir, we are happy with you. They [India] don't deserve this trophy. We love you. You are a great man. You are doing well. Keep it up,” the fan was heard saying in the video.Naqvi, who appeared to smile and wave at the supporters as his car moved past, had earlier been at the centre of the trophy presentation controversy after the Indian players did not come forward to receive the trophy from him.India had completed a dominant 72-run victory over Sri Lanka to win the Women’s Asia Cup for a record-extending eighth time. But when the presentation began, Harmanpreet Kaur and her teammates did not collect the trophy from Naqvi.Naqvi remained on the presentation stage and handed the runners-up cheque to Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu. The Indian players celebrated their title on the field but did not participate in the trophy handover involving the ACC president.As Naqvi subsequently left the stadium, “Trophy chor, trophy chor” chants were heard around the venue The chants were a callback to the controversy surrounding the men’s Asia Cup final in 2025. India had defeated Pakistan in Dubai, but the trophy and medal presentation was delayed by more than an hour, with visuals showing the Asia Cup trophy being taken away from the presentation area.The episode triggered criticism and trolling aimed at Naqvi, with “Trophy chor” subsequently becoming a recurring phrase used by some Indian supporters. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia later explained why the Indian players had refused to take the trophy from Naqvi , linking the decision to the position taken by the men’s side after last year’s Asia Cup final.“Our men’s team won the Asia Cup a year and a half ago. And our whole situation, since the April 2025 Pahalgam incident, changed after that. So, after that, there was pressure on us from our citizens that we shouldn’t keep any relations with our neighboring country and not play cricket with them. But our government has a policy that we must play against every country in multinational tournaments...”“But that doesn’t mean we will follow every condition laid out for us. Our military conflict is still ongoing. One of the main leaders who is working against the interests of our country; we can’t receive the trophy from him. The Women’s team has expressed solidarity with the decision taken by the men’s team last year,” Saikia told IANS.Naqvi had been seated in the Royal Box alongside BCCI vice-president Rajiv Shukla and Saikia during the match. Saikia insisted that the interaction between the officials was normal protocol.Saikia also revealed that efforts had been made to resolve the trophy presentation issue.“We tried to solve today's situation, but our efforts were not successful. We don’t have any regrets. Our ultimate priority and ambition was not to focus on who would give the trophy. We wanted the Indian team to win and we’ve achieved that,” he added.
Article Summary: Pakistan fan praises Mohsin Naqvi as he leaves Dubai International Cricket Stadium. Video shows Pakistan Cricket Board chairman leaving the stadium after India defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final on Sunday. India had completed a dominant 72-run victory over Sri Lanka to win the Women’s Asia Cup for a record-extending eighth time. But when the presentation began, Harmanpreet Kaur and her teammates did not collect the trophy from Naquvi.

Article Title: ‘Once in a lifetime’: Pakistan’s Salman Ali Agha answers England setback with maiden triple century
Article Text:
Salman Ali Agha

‘My form has not been good’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Salman’s triple ton puts Kingsmen in command

Just days after being sent home from Pakistan’s England tour following a disappointing start to the Test series, Salman Ali Agha has responded in emphatic fashion — with a monumental maiden first-class triple century.The Pakistan batter smashed an unbeaten 300 for Kingsmen Academy against Markhor IT Solutions in the President’s Trophy Grade-I, producing a statement innings after his omission became one of the major talking points in Pakistan cricket.Salman reached the landmark from 336 balls, hitting 42 fours and six sixes, as Kingsmen Academy declared their first innings at 565/7 in 131.1 overs at the Abbottabad Cricket Stadium.The 32-year-old also shared a mammoth 274-run partnership with Mohammad Suleman, who scored 115 off 219 balls, including 13 fours and two sixes.Salman’s extraordinary response came only days after he was sent home from England following Pakistan’s defeat in the second Test at Lord’s.Salman had entered the England tour as part of Pakistan’s Test plans and even stood in as captain in the first Test at Headingley after Babar Azam suffered an arm injury during the tour match.But his own batting struggles continued. He scored only 25 runs across two innings as Pakistan suffered an innings-and-103-run defeat at Headingley. He subsequently lost his place in the XI for the Lord’s Test and was among seven players released from the squad ahead of the third Test as Pakistan made sweeping changes after falling 0-2 behind in the series.His domestic comeback could hardly have been more emphatic.After scoring an unbeaten 101 on the opening day of the President’s Trophy, Salman returned on Sunday to turn his century into a triple century.In a video released by the Pakistan Cricket Board, Salman credited adjustments to his batting for the remarkable turnaround.“My form in international cricket has not been up to the mark in the last few series. I made slight adjustments to my batting, and I’m happy because such milestones are once in a lifetime,” Salman said.“I like to play domestic cricket, and I enjoy coming back to it, as I had spent 10 years here before graduating to the top level. I dedicate this innings to my family. My form has not been good. It was a challenging time, so I dedicate this innings to them,” he added.Salman’s innings came as Pakistan’s domestic competition provided him with the perfect platform to rebuild his confidence.Kingsmen Academy, playing in their maiden first-class tournament, resumed Sunday at 257/3 and eventually declared at 565/7 immediately after Salman completed his triple century.Markhor IT Solutions finished the day on 179/3, still 386 runs behind.Mohammad Farooq provided an explosive response with an unbeaten 107 off just 95 balls, including 11 fours and five sixes. He shared a 108-run third-wicket partnership with Atiq-ur-Rehman.But the day belonged overwhelmingly to Salman, whose stunning triple century has given the Pakistan T20I captain a timely reminder of his batting pedigree — and delivered perhaps the strongest possible response to a difficult England tour.
Article Summary: Salman Ali Agha hits maiden first-class triple century for Kingsmen Academy. The 32-year-old hit 42 fours and six sixes as Kingsmen declared their first innings at 565/7 in 131.1 overs at the Abbottabad Cricket Stadium. His extraordinary response came only days after he was sent home from England following Pakistan’s defeat in the second Test.

Article Title: ‘I just thought it was 5-1’: Alexander Zverev reveals how he missed US Open win, then calls himself the best player ‘right, right now’
Article Text:
Alexander Zverev poses for a photo with the ball boys and girls. (AP Photo)

‘I didn’t hear that she said, Game, set, match’

Zverev’s verdict on Shelton

Ben Shelton, left, and Alexander Zverev pose for a photo together with their trophies. (AP Photo)

‘Right, right now, probably yes’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Alexander Zverev had waited six years to erase the pain of his first US Open final. When the moment finally arrived, the German did not even realise he had won it.Zverev defeated American Ben Shelton 6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7, 6-2 on Sunday to win his first US Open title and second Grand Slam of the year, following his maiden major triumph at Roland Garros in June. But after sealing the championship point, the world No. 2 remained behind the baseline, preparing to receive another serve.It took his team’s reaction — and a glance around the stadium — for Zverev to realise that he was now a US Open champion.Zverev said he was so locked into the contest that he completely missed the chair umpire announcing the end of the match.“In that moment, I was in the zone a lot. I didn't hear noise at all,” Zverev said during his post-match press conference. “I was in this kind of tunnel where I just didn't hear anything. Also, when the crowd is loud, it's impossible to hear the umpire, so I didn't hear that she said, ‘Game, set, match’. At the end of the day, I just forgot the score. I just thought it was 5-1 instead of 6-2.”The victory was particularly significant for Zverev, who had lost the 2020 US Open final to Dominic Thiem after leading by two sets and being two points from the title.The German believes those scars have now finally disappeared.“I think the scars of the 2020 final, they kind of disappeared after I won in Paris,” Zverev said. “I said it at Wimbledon. Even though I lost the final, I enjoyed the match. I enjoyed being in the Grand Slam final, I enjoyed playing on Centre Court, and I enjoyed playing in front of an amazing crowd, in front of some celebrities and all that. I enjoyed doing that.”“Whereas before winning in Paris, I felt a lot of stress all the time, because there was always a question mark: ‘Will I ever win one?’ What I think now is just more of a joy to play those kinds of finals.”Shelton was playing in his first Grand Slam final, but Zverev was impressed by how much the 23-year-old had developed.“I think he's very talented, but he's very close to the hard work as well,” Zverev said. “You see him and his father all the time after matches, before matches, working on different things, and every single year he keeps improving something.”“I just played him today. I think this was the best backhand he's ever hit against me, the most consistent power. There was everything there.”Zverev recalled their first meetings and said Shelton had added a new level of consistency to his game.“I remember a couple of years ago when I first played him, he was always dangerous, he always had that serve, and he always had that forehand. But if you played three, four balls back, there would be an error, and that was absolutely not the case today.”Zverev’s second major of the season also put him in a unique position in 2026. He is the only player to have won multiple Grand Slam titles this year, while Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz have won one each.Asked whether he now considers himself the best player in the world, Zverev was reluctant to make an absolute claim — but conceded that, at this particular moment, he may have the strongest case.“I don’t know how to answer that,” he said. “You have to take everything into consideration. With Jannik Sinner being injured, Carlos Alcaraz coming back from injury after four months, right now, this moment, probably yes."“Both of them healthy, both of them at the top of their game? Maybe not. But if we say right, right now, with Jannik being injured and Carlos coming back from injury, maybe.”Sinner missed the US Open through injury, while Alcaraz returned to Grand Slam action in New York after a four-month injury layoff.Zverev, however, was quick to acknowledge that the hierarchy could look very different when all three are fully fit.“Four or five months ago, when both of them were healthy, I wasn’t [the best player in the world],” he said. “I was losing to Jannik all the time. If everyone is healthy, I think Jannik is still ahead. It’s as simple as that,” he added.Zverev is 0-5 against Sinner this year, having won just one set against the world No. 1 — a tiebreaker in the Wimbledon final.
Article Summary: Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton 6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7, 6-2 to win his first US Open title and second Grand Slam of the year. The world No. 2 did not even realise he had won the match until his team's reaction and a glance around the stadium. The German had lost the 2020 US Open final to Dominic Thiem after leading by two sets and being two points from the title.

Article Title: ‘We can’t receive the trophy from him’: Why India snubbed Mohsin Naqvi again at Women’s Asia Cup, Devajit Saikia explains
Article Text:
India’s women’s team’s decision not to receive the trophy from Mohsin Naqvi was a show of solidarity with the men’s team.

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the focus of India’s women’s cricket team moving forward? Winning more championships Building younger talent Promoting women's cricket globally 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: India’s women’s cricket team’s decision not to receive the Women’s Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naqvi was a show of solidarity with the men’s team, which took the same position after winning the Asia Cup last year, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said.“Our men’s team won the Asia Cup a year and a half ago. And our whole situation, since the April 2025 Pahalgam incident, changed after that. So, after that, there was pressure on us from our citizens that we shouldn’t keep any relations with our neighboring country and not play cricket with them. But our government has a policy that we must play against every country in multinational tournaments...” Saikia told IANS hours after India beat Sri Lanka in Sunday's final.“But that doesn’t mean we will follow every condition laid out for us. Our military conflict is still ongoing. One of the main leaders who is working against the interests of our country; we can’t receive the trophy from him. The Women’s team has expressed solidarity with the decision taken by the men’s team last year,” Saikia said.The decision brought back memories of the controversial presentation after the men's Asia Cup final in 2025. India had beaten Pakistan in the final, but the players were left waiting for more than an hour to receive the trophy and medals.This time, India had completed a comfortable 72-run victory over Sri Lanka to win a record-extending eighth Women's Asia Cup title. Harmanpreet Kaur and her teammates celebrated on the field, but the Indian side did not collect the trophy from Naqvi during the presentation.Naqvi was present at the stadium as India sealed the title and was seated alongside dignitaries including BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla and Saikia. He later went on stage and handed the runners-up cheque to Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu. The presentation then ended without India receiving the trophy from him.Saikia said the decision did not take away from the team's performance.“It doesn’t diminish the performances of our team. We have won all our matches in a one-sided manner. Women’s cricket has been growing so well in India and there’s no bigger evidence of that than this. Our whole planning is geared towards the 2026 ICC T20 World Cup. The happiest part of this tournament is how India has left everyone else behind and surged so far ahead.”The presence of Naqvi alongside Saikia and Shukla in the Royal Box during the match also led to questions about the interaction between the officials.“It’s not as if we wouldn’t meet anyone. I was sitting outside in the Royal Box seats right from the toss until the end of the game. Having sat there, I remained in that same place throughout the match. Everyone who came met me during the match; someone sat next to me, then Shukla came and sat with me. The person you mentioned also came and sat alongside Deputy Chairman Khalid (Khalid Al Zarooni) sahib. That’s just a normal tradition—whenever anyone comes, we meet and talk with everyone,” Saikia said.Saikia said there had been an attempt to resolve the trophy presentation issue.“We tried to solve today's situation, but our efforts were not successful. We don’t have any regrets. Our ultimate priority and ambition was not to focus on who would give the trophy. We wanted the Indian team to win and we’ve achieved that.”He also said his interaction with Naqvi was not centred on the trophy. Saikia had presented the fielding medal after the game and said the conversation around that was about India's next assignment.“I also got the chance to give the fielding medal that’s given out after every game. The conversation that was had around that was about the Asian Games, not about whether the trophy should be taken or not.”India's attention now shifts to the Asian Games in Japan's Aichi Prefecture. The team is scheduled to play on September 18, 20 and 22.“Currently, there are no such plans. Right now, our focus is on tomorrow, as our team will be leaving for Japan via Delhi. So, all our attention is set on the Asian Games starting in Japan, where our matches are scheduled for the 18th, 20th and 22nd. Our goal is to bring home the gold medal, and that is our sole objective.”
Article Summary: India's women's cricket team did not receive the trophy from Mohsin Naqvi. The decision was a show of solidarity with the men's team, which took the same position after winning the Asia Cup last year. Saikia said the decision did not take away from the team's performance.

Article Title: “You will inspire many more”: How Sophie Cunningham left a young Fever fan in tears with one unforgettable gesture after Indiana’s win
Article Text:
How Sophie Cunningham left a young Fever fan in tears with one unforgettable gesture after Indiana’s win(Getty)

Sophie Cunningham noticed a young fan and gave her a game-worn shoe after the Fever’s 112-98 win

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sophie Cunningham had already played her part in the Indiana Fever’s 112-98 win over the Portland Fire on Friday, August 1, 2026. But the moment that stayed with fans came after the final buzzer. Cunningham walked toward a young Fever supporter in the stands and handed her one of her game-worn shoes. The girl looked stunned, then covered her face as the emotion hit her.The Indiana Fever later shared the moment on social media, and the young fan’s reaction quickly drew attention. She did not simply take the shoe and move on. She looked at it in disbelief before becoming visibly emotional. For Cunningham, it was a quick postgame gesture. For the young supporter, it became a memory tied to a Fever win she will likely never forget.The moment came at the end of a busy night for Cunningham in Portland. She had dealt with boos from sections of the Moda Center crowd when she entered the game midway through the first quarter. Rather than let the reception affect her, she answered with a three-pointer and finished with 13 points as Indiana picked up its fifth straight victory.Then came the part nobody could have planned. After the final buzzer, Cunningham walked toward the stands and handed a young Fever fan her game-worn shoe. The child immediately looked overwhelmed. In the video shared by the Fever on August 1, she appeared to stare at the shoe in disbelief before putting her hands over her face.The Fever highlighted that exact reaction in its social media post, writing, “The reaction on this young fan’s face when Sophie Cunningham gifted her a game-worn shoe after tonight’s win in Portland.”It was a fitting way to end a night that had already given Fever fans plenty to celebrate. Indiana scored 112 points, with Caitlin Clark leading the way with 26 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists. Kelsey Mitchell also scored 26, while the Fever pulled away with a 34-point third quarter. The victory marked Indiana’s fifth consecutive win, and the team became the first in WNBA history to score at least 100 points in five straight games.But the young fan’s reaction shifted the focus from the scoreboard to something much more personal.Fever fans praised Sophie Cunningham for giving the young supporter a memory she will never forgetThe reaction did not stop with the video. Fans flooded the Fever’s post with messages praising Cunningham for taking the time to connect with a young supporter.One fan wrote, “How beautiful is this amazing woman, inside and out! For the young Fever fan, though, it became something much bigger. She left Portland with a game-worn souvenir, a special interaction with Sophie Cunningham and a story that started with a 112-98 Indiana victory.
Article Summary: Sophie Cunningham gave a young Fever fan a game-worn shoe after the Fever’s 112-98 win over the Portland Fire on Friday, August 1, 2026. The girl looked stunned, then covered her face as the emotion hit her. The Indiana Fever later shared the moment on social media.

Article Title: From Glasgow setback to Nagoya challenge, Pranati Nayak aims to get it right this time at Asian Games
Article Text:
Pranati Nayak with coach Ashok Mishra

KOLKATA: When Pranati Nayak gets ready to sprint down the runway at Nagoya City General Gymnasium during the Asian Games later this month, the memory of Glasgow will inevitably return.At the Commonwealth Games, a lack of speed in her approach disrupted her first vault in the qualifying round, costing her valuable points and, ultimately, a place in the final.It was obviously not something one is used to seeing from Nayak and even left her long-time coach Ashok Mishra at a loss for words. “It was the first time I had seen her miss the running,” said Mishra.He, however, downplayed concerns over her injury, insisting that it was not what cost her in Glasgow. She had been dealing with plantar fasciitis — a problem underneath the foot that caused some pulling while running — but had competed with it before and even won a medal this year.Despite that, coach Mishra didn’t want to take any risks and made sure she got enough rest to prepare for her fourth Asian Games appearance, where she will compete only in the vault.“It is around 90-95% cured. Just 5% remains, and that is not a problem for her,” added Mishra.“After the Commonwealth Games, I gave her around three weeks of complete rest. So, she recovered. Otherwise, if we had continued training, it could have aggravated the injury.”But more importantly, the time helped her heal mentally.“She is now mentally much more mature. After everything, we just analyse it and focus on the next,” said Mishra. Also helping her stay focused are psychologists who not only talk to her but also help her with concentration exercises.Irrespective of that, one cannot deny that age is not on her side anymore and that it does make things difficult for the 31-year-old. Still, coach Mishra is confident that Nayak is all set for the challenge.That confidence is rooted in what Nayak has achieved since contemplating walking away from the sport after the Tokyo Olympics in 2021. She has since won two Asian Championship medals, two World Cup medals and one World Challenge Cup medal for India — a run that explains why Mishra still believes she has earned her place among the country’s best.But there is no doubt that the competition will be fierce at the Asian Games.China, Japan, North and South Korea and Chinese Taipei are among the leading gymnastics nations in the continent, while countries such as Philippines and Malaysia have also strengthened their programmes. The Korean gymnasts, in particular, are expected to pose a major challenge on vault.“It’s going to be a very difficult test for her. But I think she will do well. If she does both the 360-degree twist vaults cleanly with a fixed landing, then there is a very good possibility of her going to the final because execution matters,” said Mishra.Keeping this in mind, the coach has centred her training on reducing executional errors and improving explosive strength. To make sure she can do that, Nayak has been working on plyometrics, explosive leg-strength exercises and isometric muscle contractions.She has also been training on soft-landing equipment and in the foam pit, where the physical impact is reduced, before making the transition to the main landing area.For Mishra, that transition is as much mental as physical. “When it comes to the main landing area, it is much more difficult psychologically. You think about how heavy the impact will be,” he said.Nayak certainly has enough experience to make that shift at the right moment. After all, she remains India’s lone gymnast at the Asian Games for the second time in a row. And when she makes that run in Nagoya, the objective will be simple: get the approach right, execute the vault cleanly and, this time, make it to the final.
Article Summary: At the Commonwealth Games, a lack of speed in her approach disrupted her first vault in the qualifying round, costing her valuable points and, ultimately, a place in the final. She had been dealing with plantar fasciitis but had competed with it before and even won a medal this year.

NEW DELHI: India women's cricket team vice-captain Smriti Mandhana is one of the biggest names in women's cricket. Over the years, she has become one of the key players for India and has inspired many young cricketers with her batting and leadership.However, while her cricket career has continued to grow, Mandhana has also gone through a difficult phase in her personal life. Her marriage was called off last year.Mandhana has not spoken publicly about Palash Muchhal , the man she was supposed to marry. During a recent podcast with Shamani, she was asked about the hardest night of her life.Mandhana took a long pause before making it clear that she wanted to speak only about cricket.During the conversation, Shamani asked Mandhana a direct question."When was the last time you cried??" Shamani asked.Mandhana appeared emotional and paused for several seconds before answering the question."Good question. I don't remember. You know, I cry for movies. I don't cry for my real life," Mandhana said.The India star then spoke about a movie that made her emotional."If I watch a movie, I cry. So I think I was watching Mosafir Cafe and it just got me emotional, happy emotional.And I cried," she said.Mandhana then explained why the movie made her emotional."It was very nice. Not even. I got very happy emotion. I was like, yeah, man. I also want to do something like just leave everything, just," she said.Mandhana has largely stayed away from discussing her personal life in public after her marriage was called off.Even during the podcast, she chose to keep the conversation focused on her cricket journey when asked about the difficult period in her life.The India opener now faces another big challenge as India take on Sri Lanka in the Women's Asia Cup final in Dubai.Former India men's cricketer Vivek Razdan believes Mandhana will be one of the most important players for India in the final.India enter Sunday's final as favourites, but defending champions Sri Lanka cannot be taken lightly after their comeback win over Pakistan in the semifinal."The Indian team is a very strong team. But you can't underestimate Sri Lanka, especially the way they played against Pakistan. After being 33/4, they chased down the required target. Despite Athapaththu being out early, you can see how much batting depth the team has," Razdan told IANS in a virtual interaction organised by Sony Sports Network.Razdan also praised India's bowling attack, which has played an important role in the tournament. He, however, wants Mandhana to focus on her own strengths instead of trying to match the aggressive approach of Shafali Verma.Shafali and Mandhana have been India's main run-scorers in the tournament so far, with 168 and 154 runs respectively.Razdan said India need to improve their batting in the powerplay and highlighted the importance of Mandhana staying at the crease for a long time."The Indian team bowling line-up is very strong. You can talk about N Sree Charni, Shafali, or Deepti. All of them have been very strong in these games. But there is one thing that needs to be worked on - how do you bat in powerplay?"In the last game, Shafali scored a fifty against Bangladesh, but she survived three dropped catches and one run-out chance. Regarding Smriti Mandhana, it is very important for her to play for a long time. I don't know why, but I feel that Smriti sometimes tries to be Shafali. That's not her game."Razdan believes India can put up a big total if the top order avoids losing wickets early.With India's middle and lower order capable of finishing strongly, he feels Mandhana's role at the top could prove decisive on Dubai's slow pitches."If you can play the powerplay without losing a wicket, you will be able to post a big score because all of this depends on the top four. We have some batters who can help you at the back end. But if you want to win the match and the final, I will have a special eye on someone to do it, and it will be Smriti Mandhana."
Article Summary: Vivek Razdan wants Smriti Mandhana to play her natural game. Former India men's cricketer says India need to improve batting in powerplay. India take on Sri Lanka in the Women's Asia Cup final in Dubai on Sunday.

Article Title: 'He shouldn't be here': Nasser Hussain bashes Pakistan with Virender Sehwag example

Former England captain Nasser Hussain has slammed Pakistan’s decision to bring Saim Ayub into the Test team straight from the Caribbean Premier League (CPL), saying the young batter “shouldn't be here”.Ayub’s return to the Pakistan Test team ended in a nightmare as he was dismissed for a duck in both innings of the third Test against England at Edgbaston. The young opener faced only 11 balls across the two innings, with England pacer Ollie Robinson dismissing him on both occasions.Ayub had arrived in England after playing T20 cricket in the CPL. Hussain questioned why Pakistan chose to bring him into a Test match without enough preparation for the conditions.Speaking on Sky Sports after Pakistan finished Day 2 at 52-2 in their second innings, Hussain said Ayub should not have been picked for the Test.“The truth is he shouldn't be here. He came from the CPL and hasn't played first-class cricket in some time,” Hussain said during a post-day show on Sky Sports.Hussain said bringing a player directly from T20 cricket into a Test in England was a poor decision.“I don't know who thinks it's the right thing to fly someone over from foreign conditions, playing a completely different format, and think they're going to be fine in these conditions against a Dukes ball, against Ollie Robinson and England's bowling attack,” Hussain asserted, explaining why Ayub was destined to fail in these conditions against a team of the calibre of England.Hussain also recalled what happened when India once took a similar approach with Virender Sehwag Sehwag was flown into England without enough match practice and struggled at the same ground. Hussain said that if even a player of Sehwag’s experience could struggle, Pakistan should not have expected Ayub to immediately succeed.“Virender Sehwag tried it on this ground, if you remember... they flew him in. Virender Sehwag got a pair, and that's Virender Sehwag, who's a better, more experienced player than Saim,” highlighted Hussain.Hussain said Ayub must take some responsibility for the shot he played, but he questioned the decision-makers who selected him.“So a bit of responsibility goes to the lad for the shot he played. But also, whoever thought that was a seriously good decision and that he was going to go okay this week?”“It is just a sort of disrespect and disregard for Test match cricket. Test match cricket, as any cricketer will tell you, is the toughest format. Batting at the top of the order in England is the toughest task, and you just feel you can fly someone in from some part of the world and go, Good luck,” he said.
Article Summary: Saim Ayub was dismissed for a duck in both innings of the third Test against England at Edgbaston. The young opener faced only 11 balls across the two innings, with England pacer Ollie Robinson dismissing him on both occasions. Hussain questioned why Pakistan chose to bring him into a Test match without enough preparation for the conditions.

MUMBAI: In a first, the iconic Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India here will be the home venue of Railways in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy In the past, the Railways have played their home Ranji Trophy matches at the Karnail Singh Stadium in New Delhi.Placed in Elite Group D, Railways will play their three 2026-27 Ranji Trophy home ties at the Brabourne Stadium-their season-the opening match against Uttarakhand from Oct 11-14, the big game against 42-time champions Mumbai (it will be an away game for Mumbai!) from Nov 2-5, and then against Haryana from Jan 17-20.This will be the first time the Brabourne Stadium will stage a Ranji Trophy match in more than three years. The historic venue last staged a Ranji Trophy match between Mumbai and Maharashtra from Jan 24-27, 2023. The match ended in a draw."I'm truly happy that the Ranji Trophy is returning to the CCI. The Brabourne Stadium has staged the maximum number of Ranji Trophy finals (16) in India. There's a replica of the Ranji Trophy in the CCI main hall, which was kept by former BCCI and CCI president Raj Singh Dungarpur many years back.So, there has always been a special and cherished relationship between Brabourne stadium CCI's senior member and well-known cricket lover Sachin Bajaj told TOI on Saturday."My old friend Syed Zakaria Zuffri (former Assam and Railways ‘keeper-batsman and current Railways head coach) requested to me if the CCI could stage Railways' home Ranji Trophy matches in the upcoming season. I asked him to contact CCI's Cricket committee vice-chairman Mayank Khandwala in this regard. I must appreciate the efforts of Mayank and the CCI cricket committee in making this happen," he added."It is a matter of immense pride and great emotion for all of us at the Cricket Club of India to welcome the Ranji Trophy back to Brabourne Stadium after a significant interval. Cricket at CCI is not merely a sport, it is part of the Club’s identity, its heritage and its soul. For generations, Brabourne Stadium has witnessed some of the finest moments in Indian cricket and has been privileged to host legendary players, great teams and memorable encounters. The Ranji Trophy has always held a very special place in that extraordinary history. The return of first-class cricket to CCI is therefore much more than the staging of a few matches. It is the revival of a proud cricketing tradition and the reopening of a historic chapter. We are particularly delighted that Railways have chosen CCI as their home ground. We are honoured to partner with them and are committed to providing the players, officials and spectators with the very best facilities and an environment befitting the stature of the Ranji Trophy," Khandwala told TOI."As the vice-chairman of the Cricket Committee at CCI, I believe strongly that our responsibility is not only to preserve the magnificent cricketing legacy of this institution, but also to keep that legacy alive for the next generation. Bringing premier domestic cricket back to Brabourne is an important part of that vision. The Ranji Trophy represents the foundation of Indian cricket. It is where talent is tested, characters are built and future international stars begin their journey. To have that journey once again unfolding at CCI is something we should all celebrate. The Brabourne Stadium has a history that speaks for itself. Now, we look forward to creating the next chapter. On behalf of CCI, we extend a warm welcome to Railways, the players, support staff, match officials, the BCCI and, most importantly, cricket lovers who will return to CCI to experience the magic of first-class cricket. The Ranji Trophy is coming home to CCI. The heritage continues, and the next chapter begins," he added.The Railways team playing its home ties in the Ranji Trophy in the upcoming season is another step forward in cricket returning to CCI. Earlier this month, the International Cricket Council had announced that India will stage the inaugural edition of the six-team inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027, with matches scheduled between 14-28 Feb, 2027 at the Brabourne Stadium in Mumbai and the Kotambi Stadium Vadodara.It’s learnt that the CCI is currently installing new floodlights at the Brabourne Stadium. “We are in the process of installing new floodlights at the stadium. We’ll commission the new lights by Oct 10-15,” Khandwala said.The Railways have clinched the coveted Ranji Trophy twice in the past -in 2001–02 and 2004–05. However, they've met with little success in recent years, and failed to move beyond the league stage of the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy, finishing fourth in Elite Group C with 23 points in seven matches.
Article Summary: The iconic Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India will be the home venue of Railways in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy. The historic venue last staged a Ranji trophy match between Mumbai and Maharashtra from Jan 24-27, 2023.

Chennai: Tilak Varma was finally dismissed in this year’s Duleep Trophy, falling agonisingly short of a second century. Despite being dismissed for 99, the South Zone captain’s red-ball ambitions stay intact, even though his team is staring at a big loss against East at the MA Chidambaram Stadium.Tilak, who had scored a century and a half-century in South Zone’s semifinal win against North Zone without being dismissed, battled through the Chennai heat on Wednesday against a quality East Zone attack. He was the last man to fall, giving a return catch to off-spinner Kounain Quraishi, as South were eventually bowled out for 336, conceding a massive 372-run first-innings lead.East, opting to bat again rather than send their bowlers back out, were 212-5 at stumps on Day Four, stretching their lead to 584.For Tilak, however, the larger picture remained clear. The 23-year-old left-hander has made no secret about his desire to play Test cricket for India.“I always say to everyone that I want to play red-ball cricket for India, that’s my biggest goal. As a kid, I thought I would play Test cricket first and then white-ball cricket. Red-ball cricket has always been my favourite, it’s my ‘A’ game,” Tilak said.“Over the last five-six years, I have played a lot of white-ball cricket and become good at it.Red-ball cricket is still my favourite, but I am comfortable with both now,” said Tilak.Tilak resumed the day on 56 and immediately took the attack to Mohammed Shami (2-42), striking two boundaries in the opening over. He and Chama Milind took 44 runs from the nine overs of Shami and Mukesh Kumar’s (3-62) combined first spell, putting them under pressure.Shami conceded 25 in his first four overs after giving away only 17 in 11 overs on Day 3.Kishan breaks 16-year-old recordEast’s second innings saw Ishan Kishan continue his first-innings form with 80 off 98 balls, while Shikhar Mohan (52) also remained among the runs.Ishan Kishan amassed 350 runs across both innings of the Duleep Trophy final, surpassing Dinesh Karthik’s aggregate of 333 runs from the 2010 final to set a new record for the most runs in the tournament final.Brief scores: East Zone 708 & 212-5 (I Kishan 80, S Mohan 52; Md Siraj 1-17) vs South Zone 336 (T Varma 99; M Kumar 3-62, Md Shami 2-42, M Quraishi 2-99).
Article Summary: South Zone captain Tilak Varma finally dismissed in Duleep Trophy final. South bowled out for 336, conceding 372-run first-innings lead to East. East opting to bat again rather than send bowlers back out, were 212-5 at stumps.

Article Title: ‘Focus on wearing your national cap, education, respect your parents and coaches’: Arjuna Ranatunga tells Mumbai' budding cricketers
Article Text:
File Photo: Arjuna Ranatunga (TOI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Sri Lanka's celebrated 1996 World Cup winning captain Arjuna Ranatunga is in Mumbai these days, on a 'business visit.'Ranatunga arrived in the city on Friday with his close friend and businessman Venkatesh K Rao. On Saturday, the 62-year-old Lankan great addressed a gathering of budding cricketers and their parents, of the Payyade Sports Club in Kandivli.“I had the privilege of having a good session with young cricketers of Mumbai yesterday. I spoke to them about some of the cricketing values which are missing today. I told them about the value of technique, something that you could see in my playing time with the likes of Sachin Tendulkar, Mohammed Azharuddin, Sourav Ganguly and other top Indian batters,” Ranatunga told TOI on Sunday.The former left-hander, who scored 5105 runs in 93 Tests, asserted that it was important to teach today’s young cricketers about the value of playing for the country, rather than only focus on raking in moolah by playing in cash-rich franchise T20 leagues.“It's important to bring these kids on the right track. Today's cricketers look to play in the franchise leagues, rather than playing for their country. They are looking at the financial benefits, rather than taking pride in wearing the cap and jersey of your national team.If you look at it, a couple of Sri Lankan cricketers missed Sri Lanka's series recently to play in franchise cricket, and in India's case too, cricketers are prioritising playing for their franchises.The cricket boards also need to look at the need of their cricketers playing for the country. I'm not saying get rid of T20 cricket, but back in Colombo too, I look to emphasize on the importance of educating the budding cricketers about the value of playing Test cricket," Ranatunga explained."It is the seniors who need to show the way, make a little bit of sacrifice. So, we emphasized on that. Dr Shetty also has the same ideas that I carry. Before I started my speech, he said a lot of things that I was supposed to mention in my speech. Both of us spoke about the value of wearing the national cap, maintaining discipline, the value of education and technique, respecting your parents and coaches-those are the things that are missing in cricket today, and we need to educate the kids about it," he stressed."I enjoyed talking to the cricketers, they listened to me very attentively. We were lucky that growing up, we had our role models in Sunil Gavaskar and Gundappa Viswanath.When we went to Pakistan, we saw some fine cricketing brains like Imran Khan, Javed Miandad and Abdul Qadir. When I played a Test for the first time in India, in Chennai, Gavaskar took time out for us and spoke to us in our dressing room after the match. I will always cherish his words that day," Ranatunga said."It was a very good session, which lasted for 90 minutes. He was talking about cricket and how to respect parents and how to leave the house with the blessing of your parents. He also told the kids to focus on studies. He told the cricketers that they should focus on education too because today, a cricketer has to be intelligent as well. He emphasized to the aspiring cricketers that studies and parents' respect is very important," Payyade Sports Club president and former MCA joint secretary PV Shetty told Mumbai Mirror.Gaurav Payyade, former MCA apex council member and secretary of Payyade SC, and Bhushan Patil, member of MCA’s present Apex Council, were also present on the occasion."We wanted him to speak to the boys at the ground, but it was raining. So, he spoke to the young cricketers of our club at my hotel in Kandivali. He is keen to establish a cricket academy in Mumbai in collaboration with me," Shetty said.Ranataunga and Venkatesh will leave for Rajkot on Wednesday as they have to visit Morbi for business purposes.
Article Summary: Sri Lanka's 1996 World Cup winning captain Arjuna Ranatunga is in Mumbai on a 'business visit' The 62-year-old Lankan great addressed a gathering of budding cricketers and their parents. He said it was important to teach today’s young cricketer about the value of playing for the country.

Article Title: Women’s Asia Cup: Shafali, Smriti’s stunning opening act powers India to eighth title
Article Text:
Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brief scores: India Women 183/5 in 20 overs (S Verma 68, S Mandhana 59; C Praboda 1/40) beat Sri Lanka Women 111 all out in 20 overs (C Athapaththu 36, N Silva 22; S Charani 4-20, D Sharma 3-19) by 72 runs.

At last, India got a batting beauty and made the most of it, thanks to their in-form openers Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana . Continuing her blazing form, Shafali smashed 68 off 39, adding 129 in just 77 balls with fellow superstar and vice-captain Mandhana (59 off 39), who also stroked a half-century, as India defeated defending champions Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Women’s Asia Cup final to clinch a record eighth title at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday. Shree Charani snapped four wickets to hasten Sri Lanka’s downfall.In a murderous mood, Shafali took just 24 balls to reach her 21st fifty, erasing Mandhana’s 25-ball effort in 2022 as the fastest fifty in Women’s Asia Cup history. Mandhana reached her 36th T20I half century in 35 balls. Given the start they got, India would be disappointed at not reaching 200 after a middle-order muddle. Skipper Harmanpreet Kaur (14, 14b, 1x4), Richa Ghosh (17, 13b, 1x4, 1x6) and Deepti Sharma (5, 7b) fell cheaply as Sri Lanka staged a fine fightback.India recovered towards the end through a fine cameo from G Kamalini (15*, 5b, 1x4, 1x6), who was surprisingly included in the XI after India dropped out-of-form No. 3 Pratika Rawal. Kamalini skipped down the track to edge Sugandika Kumari for four before finishing the innings in style by dancing down the track and depositing the bowler over cow corner. Sri Lanka also suffered a major blow when batter Vishmi Gunarathne was stretchered off after twisting her ankle while fielding.The injury leaves the pressure of a stiff 184-run chase on captain Chamari Athapaththu and her team.Shafali, who cracked her third half century of the tournament — all three scores have been in the 60s — and Mandhana took the Sri Lankan attack to the cleaners on perhaps the best batting surface of the tournament. With 236 runs in five matches at 47.20 and a strike rate of 171.01, Shafali is set to finish as the tournament’s leading run-scorer. Mandhana, with 213 runs at 42.60 and a strike rate of 165.11, is set to finish second.Shafali targeted Athapaththu in the latter’s first over, creaming her for 6, 6 and 4 as the Sri Lankan skipper conceded 20 runs. India raced to 57 in the Powerplay and reached 98 at the halfway mark without losing a wicket. Much to Sri Lanka’s relief, the stand ended when Shafali slapped Praboda straight to Athapaththu at the edge of the circle.Mandhana, though, would be disappointed to have been run out for the third time in this Asia Cup. In a debatable decision, she sacrificed her wicket in the 14th over after Harmanpreet cut a ball to point and set off, leaving her partner with little option but to go through with the run. It was a poor call by Harmanpreet, though Mandhana could have turned it down.
Article Summary: India beat Sri Lanka Women by 72 runs in the Women's Asia Cup final. Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana both scored half-centuries. Verma took just 24 balls to reach her 21st fifty. Sri Lanka suffered a major blow when Vishmi Gunarathne was stretchered off.

Article Title: India thrive in home comfort: Bumrah hits stride on comeback as Iyer’s men crush Afghanistan in first T20I
Article Text:
India's captain Shreyas Iyer, second right, shakes hands with Afghanistan players. (PTI Photo)

Brief scores: Afghanistan 156-8 in 20 overs (Azmatullah Omarzai 64 not out, Mohammad Nabi 33; Arshdeep Singh 3-19, Varun Chakravarthy 1-16) lost to India 157-3 in 13.4 overs (Abhishek Sharma 82, Ishan Kishan 42; Mohammad Nabi 2-28) by seven wickets.

NEW DELHI: Jasprit Bumrah ’s first delivery of the night drifted past Rahmanullah Gurbaz’s pads and beat wicketkeeper Sanju Samson to the boundary for five wides. That was the only time one could say he was coming off an injury layoff. Two deliveries later, he got the ball to kick from a good length for Gurbaz to awkwardly fend it to first slip. From there, usual business resumed for India’s T20I team on home soil after a winless tour of Ireland and England two months ago.The Indian bowling attack, led by Bumrah, stifled Afghanistan to 156/8.Opener Abhishek Sharma effortlessly blazed away to 82 off 32 and Ishan Kishan eased to 42 off 33 as India cantered to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series with seven wickets and 38 balls to spare with captain Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma completing the formalities at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on Sunday evening.On paper, Afghanistan are the hosts of this T20I series. But the Indian T20I team re-established this as their hunting ground. As is often the case with Bumrah, that one menacing delivery to Gurbaz shook the confidence of the Afghanistan batting. And as usual, Bumrah set the tone for the rest of the attack to settle down on a length against an unsure batting lineup.Call it the impact of Bumrah’s spell of 1/26 or playing in Indian conditions, India’s new T20I captain Iyer finally got to see how ominous this team can be after taking over the reins from Suryakumar Yadav post the T20 World Cup triumph at home.Azmatullah Omarzai’s enterprising unbeaten 64 off 44 balls dragged Afghanistan out of the ditch at 43/5 to post 156/8. Bumrah’s arrival just goes to show the difference he makes to an attack.Going by their records, Arshdeep Singh, Axar Patel and Varun Chakravarthy were expected to have the upper hand against a comparatively inexperienced Afghan batting lineup. That said, this same attack without Bumrah came second in all six T20Is on the tour of Ireland and England.The incisive opening burst allowed Arshdeep, Axar and Varun to apply the choke as they returned figures of 3/19, 1/27 and 1/16.Bumrah has predominantly played T20 cricket over last year. Most of it has been on scary flat decks. Sunday’s pitch at the Ferozeshah Kotla was a tired one after enduring the load of the IPL and Delhi Premier League T20.Help of any kind from the surface is enough for Bumrah to get into the minds of the batters. From letting it rip with the new ball to using the dual nature of the pitch with his cutters, he flaunted his wares in his first T20 game after the IPL. If one crack in India’s T20 cricket stood exposed on Sunday night, it was the lack of decent bowling allrounder. Even as Omarzai went about rebuilding the innings with veteran Mohammed Nabi, the run rate dipped below six runs per over by the 10th over with India’s frontline bowlers operating with immaculate accuracy. The shackles were broken only when seamers Nitish Kumar Reddy and Shivam Dube were taken for 0/30 in two overs and 21 off one over respectively.
Article Summary: India take 1-0 lead in three-match series with seven wickets and 38 balls to spare. Jasprit Bumrah took 1/26 in his first T20 game after injury layoff. Abhishek Sharma hit 82 and Ishan Kishan 42 as India reached 157-3 in 13.4 overs.

Article Title: ‘Proud moment for Indian cricket’: PM Modi, President Murmu hail India after historic Women’s Asia Cup triumph
Article Text:
PM Modi congratulates Team India

‘A proud moment for Indian cricket ’: PM Modi congratulates Team India

Shukla, Dhami and Puri hail dominant campaign

Saikia explains India’s decision over trophy presentation

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Droupadi Murmu led the tributes on Monday as India celebrated the women’s eighth Women’s Asia Cup title, with both praising Harmanpreet Kaur ’s side for an unbeaten and dominant campaign.India defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday to extend their record in the continental tournament. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma powered India to 183/5 before Sree Charani and Deepti Sharma spearheaded a disciplined bowling effort that restricted Sri Lanka to 111.The triumph prompted congratulatory messages from across the country, with Modi highlighting the confidence and consistency shown by the side throughout the tournament.“A proud moment for Indian cricket! Congratulations to the Women’s team on winning the Asia Cup. Their confidence, consistency and remarkable spirit were on full display throughout the tournament. May this triumph inspire millions of youngsters across the country to play more and shine,” PM Modi wrote on X.President Droupadi Murmu also congratulated the players, describing the achievement as a source of inspiration, particularly for young women.“My heartiest congratulations to all the members of Team India on winning Women’s T20 Asia Cup Championship 2026. They played superbly as a team throughout the tournament, winning all the matches. They have done the country proud. They are a source of great inspiration for our youth, especially our daughters. I am sure, they will script many more inspiring chapters of success and excellence,” the President’s official handle posted on X.BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla also praised the team for maintaining an unbeaten record and credited every member for contributing to the title.“What a performance by our Women in Blue! Undefeated throughout the tournament and now Asia Cup champions for the 8th time Every player stepped up when required. A complete team effort and a proud moment for Indian cricket. Well played, Team India!” Shukla wrote on X.Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami praised the side’s discipline and confidence, calling the achievement a matter of pride for the country.Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas Hardeep Singh Puri also lauded India’s all-round display.“What a day it was for Indian sports! Another big win for India! A dominating show by Team India to defeat Sri Lanka by 72 runs to lift the Women’s Asia Cup Cricket 2026 in Dubai for a record eight time! Batting brilliance. Bowling firepower. Electric fielding. Nerves of steel. Every department fired. Every moment belonged to India. Take a bow, Champions! You’ve made the tricolour fly higher and a billion cheers roar louder!” Puri wrote on X.India’s victory was built around a record 129-run opening partnership between Mandhana and Shafali. Mandhana scored 59 off 39 balls, while Shafali made 68 off 39. Sree Charani then claimed 4/20 and Deepti Sharma returned 3/19 as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 111.The celebrations were accompanied by a politically sensitive moment during the trophy presentation, as India did not receive the Women’s Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naqvi.“Our men’s team won the Asia Cup a year and a half ago. And our whole situation, since the April 2025 Pahalgam incident, changed after that. So, after that, there was pressure on us from our citizens that we shouldn’t keep any relations with our neighboring country and not play cricket with them. But our government has a policy that we must play against every country in multinational tournaments...” Saikia told IANS.“But that doesn’t mean we will follow every condition laid out for us. Our military conflict is still ongoing. One of the main leaders who is working against the interests of our country; we can’t receive the trophy from him. The Women’s team has expressed solidarity with the decision taken by the men’s team last year,” he said.Saikia stressed that the decision did not diminish the achievement.“It doesn’t diminish the performances of our team. We have won all our matches in a one-sided manner. Women’s cricket has been growing so well in India and there’s no bigger evidence of that than this. Our whole planning is geared towards the 2026 ICC T20 World Cup. The happiest part of this tournament is how India has left everyone else behind and surged so far ahead.”India’s focus now shifts to the Asian Games in Japan’s Aichi Prefecture, with Saikia saying the team’s immediate objective is clear.“Currently, there are no such plans. Right now, our focus is on tomorrow, as our team will be leaving for Japan via Delhi. So, all our attention is set on the Asian Games starting in Japan, where our matches are scheduled for the 18th, 20th and 22nd. Our goal is to bring home the gold medal, and that is our sole objective.”
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi and President Droupadi Murmu lead tributes as India celebrate Women's Asia Cup title. India defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma powered India to 183/5 before Sree Charani and Deepti Sharma spearheaded a disciplined bowling effort.

Article Title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi on the bench: Why India's bold T20I vision feels incomplete
Article Text:
Gautam Gambhir with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi during practice session; Sanju Samson during the first T20I vs Afghanistan. (PTI/ANI Photos)

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (ANI Photo)

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (PTI Photo)

NEW DELHI: India T20I skipper Shreyas Iyer called having to pick between Sanju Samson , Vaibhav Sooryanshi and Abhishek Sharma as a "luxury to have for any side." More often than not, the challenge is to pick between Samson and Sooryavanshi. One brings experience, and the other brings a no-holds-barred approach.That was the case as the T20I series between India and Afghanistan got underway on Sunday at the Arun Jaitley Stadium. No clear signs of one or the other emerged as the teams went through the motions. Abhishek did some shadow batting. Sooryavanshi lined up to take some aerial catches. India coach Gautam Gambhir pinged Samson's wicketkeeping gloves.As the team went into a huddle and emerged, both Samson and Sooryavanshi found their way onto the dugout. Both kept their poker faces well. Ishan Kishan, one of the wicketkeeping options in the squad, spoke for a considerable period with batting coach Sitanshu Kotak.The mystery box was opened at the toss when Shreyas Iyer announced that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Washington Sundar and two more (Ravi Bishnoi and Yash Thakur) were not in the playing XI. His reasoning to Sanjay Manjrekar was near incoherent."That is more difficult, I feel, but I would say if Vaibhav (Sooryavanshi) is not playing, then Washington (Sundar) is not playing and there are two more which you'll get to know," he said on managing team combinations and selecting players for the match.When it came to it, Sanju Samson scored just 10 runs from 8 balls with two boundaries to show for it. His brief stay in the middle was halted by Azmatullah Omarzai, giving catching practice to Darwish Rasooli at deep square leg in the process. On a surface that needed patience before getting going, as Abhishek Sharma demonstrated with a 32-ball 82, the 31-year-old had not made the most of the opportunity.The question of batting order that Iyer didn't answer with conviction at the toss was probed again with Abhishek Sharma and Varun Chakaravarthy after India's 7-wicket win with 38 balls to spare."I still remember two years back, we decided we want to play a certain way and dominate all teams. It worked for a year. But one or two (bad) series won't define our batting. As openers, you want to give a good start as an opener," said Sharma, whose 82-run knock earned him the Player of the Match.Varun, meanwhile, praised India's top order for how lethal they are against spinners."Against our team, batting line-up, you can't bowl spin. So, if you bowl spin against our batting line-up, they are just going to smack (you) left, right and centre. We are so used to playing spinners. We have one of the best batting line-ups and our top-8 can take on any spinner in the world. I have personally bowled against them, played against them. I know how hard it is. So, yeah, I feel for the spinners," said the spinner who had an economical return from injury.The question, however, persists over Sooryavanshi's place in the team and the long-term approach in the format. Samson's presence adds a wicketkeeping option and a left-right pairing at the top of the order. But, with all due respect to Samson's abilities, it steals what can be a game-changing and game-deciding pairing of Abhishek-Sooryavanshi.Samson posted single-digit scores against Ireland and in the first T20I against England before allowing Sooryavanshi to come in and make his India debut. Sooryavanshi couldn't do much either, with 42 runs from three matches.But as Samson was rested for the tour to Zimbabwe and Sooryavanshi became the de facto choice, the 15-year-old produced a series-topping 151 runs from three matches at a strike rate of 196.10.With India set to play two T20Is against Afghanistan, a one-off T20I against Japan, the Asian Games, five T20Is against West Indies, five T20Is against New Zealand and three T20Is against Sri Lanka in 2026, the can of worms involving Sooryavanshi has been opened with his absence.The sole reason Sooryavanshi was included in squads for Ireland and England, and fast-tracked into the Indian team at all of 15, was to give wings to this sensational talent. Not playing him, in favour of Samson's experience, does grave disservice to him, his talent and Indian cricket at large.
Article Summary: India beat Afghanistan by seven wickets in the first T20I in Delhi. India captain Shreyas Iyer has to pick between Sanju Samson, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma. India coach Gautam Gambhir pinged Samson's wicketkeeping gloves.

Article Title: ‘Trophy chor’ comes back again: Fans chant at Mohsin Naqvi after India women’s Asia Cup triumph

‘Trophy chor, trophy chor’ echoed around the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday as Mohsin Naqvi walked away from the presentation dais after India’s 72-run win over Sri Lanka in the Women’s Asia Cup final.India had secured a record-extending eighth Women’s Asia Cup title, but Harmanpreet Kaur and her teammates did not collect the trophy from Naqvi, the Asian Cricket Council president and Pakistan Cricket Board chairman.Naqvi remained on the presentation stage and handed the runners-up cheque to Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu. The Indian team did not come forward to receive the trophy from him, and Naqvi had to leave the stadium without handing over the trophy.The chant was a callback to the controversy that followed the men’s Asia Cup final in 2025.India had defeated Pakistan in the final in Dubai, but the post-match presentation was delayed by more than an hour. The Indian players were left waiting for their trophy and medals, while visuals showed the Asia Cup trophy being taken away from the presentation area.The episode triggered a wave of criticism and trolling aimed at Naqvi, with ‘Trophy chor’ becoming a recurring label used against him.The same chant was heard at the Dubai stadium on Sunday when he was leaving the stadium after the Indian women declined to receive the trophy from Naqvi.“Our men’s team won the Asia Cup a year and a half ago. And our whole situation, since the April 2025 Pahalgam incident, changed after that. So, after that, there was pressure on us from our citizens that we shouldn’t keep any relations with our neighboring country and not play cricket with them. But our government has a policy that we must play against every country in multinational tournaments...”“But that doesn’t mean we will follow every condition laid out for us. Our military conflict is still ongoing. One of the main leaders who is working against the interests of our country; we can’t receive the trophy from him. The Women’s team has expressed solidarity with the decision taken by the men’s team last year,” Saikia told IANS.Naqvi had been seated in the Royal Box alongside BCCI vice-president Rajiv Shukla and Saikia during the match. The visuals of the officials speaking with Naqvi also drew attention after the presentation.Saikia said the interaction was part of the normal protocol during the match.“It’s not as if we wouldn’t meet anyone. I was sitting outside in the Royal Box seats right from the toss until the end of the game. Having sat there, I remained in that same place throughout the match. Everyone who came met me during the match; someone sat next to me, then Shukla came and sat with me. The person you mentioned also came and sat alongside Deputy Chairman Khalid (Khalid Al Zarooni) sahib. That’s just a normal tradition—whenever anyone comes, we meet and talk with everyone. ”Saikia said an effort had been made to resolve the trophy presentation issue, but it did not succeed.“We tried to solve today's situation, but our efforts were not successful. We don’t have any regrets. Our ultimate priority and ambition was not to focus on who would give the trophy. We wanted the Indian team to win and we’ve achieved that.”
Article Summary: Mohsin Naqvi left the Dubai International Cricket Stadium without handing over the trophy. The chant was a callback to the controversy that followed the men’s Asia Cup final in 2025. India had defeated Pakistan in the final in Dubai, but the post-match presentation was delayed.

Article Title: ‘We are the champions’: Amol Muzumdar backs BCCI stand as India skip Women’s Asia Cup trophy presentation with Mohsin Naqvi

Team India after winning the Women's Asia Cup 2026. (Pic credit: BCCI)

India dominate Sri Lanka to win eighth title
